title: 떡보와 사신
titleT: The Rice-Cake Eater and the Envoy

pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 한 마을에 떡을 세상에서 제일 좋아하는 총각이 살았어요. 이름은 아무도 몰랐어요. 다들 그냥 "떡보"라고 불렀지요. 오늘도 떡보는 허리춤에 커다란 나무 주걱을 쓱 꽂고, 떡메를 번쩍 들고 노래를 불렀답니다. "떡 하나 쿵! 떡 둘 쿵! 세어 보자, 배가 통통!"
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a certain village, there lived a young man who loved rice cakes more than anything else in the whole wide world. Nobody knew his real name. Everyone just called him Tteokbo, the Rice-Cake Boy. Today, too, Tteokbo tucked a great big wooden paddle into his belt, swung his rice-cake mallet high, and sang. "One rice cake, thump! Two rice cakes, thump! Count them up — my belly goes plump!"

pages.ko: 그 무렵 궁궐에서는 큰일이 났어요. 바다 건너 먼 나라에서 사신이 찾아왔거든요. 그런데 이 손님, 입을 꾹 다물고 한마디도 하지 않았어요. 대신 손짓으로만 어려운 문제를 척척 냈지요.
pages.t: Just about then, something big was happening at the palace. An envoy had come all the way from a faraway land across the sea. But this guest kept his mouth shut tight and would not say one single word. Instead, he asked hard, hard questions using only his hands.

pages.ko: "저 손짓이 대체 무슨 뜻이냐?" 임금님이 물었어요. 하지만 신하들은 서로 얼굴만 멀뚱멀뚱 쳐다보았지요. 수염을 배배 꼬고, 이마를 긁적긁적. "으음…" "그, 글쎄올시다…" 아무도 답을 몰랐답니다.
pages.t: "What on earth do those hand signs mean?" asked the king. But the ministers only stared blankly at one another. They twisted their beards round and round and scratched their foreheads. "Hmmm…" "W-well, you see…" Not one of them knew the answer.

pages.ko: 바로 그때, 궁궐 부엌에 시루를 지고 온 떡보가 문틈으로 목을 쭉 빼고 구경을 했어요. "손짓이라면 저도 좀 하는뎁쇼?" 늙은 신하의 눈이 번쩍 뜨였어요. "옳지! 자네가 한번 나서 보게!" 떡보는 초립을 꾹 고쳐 쓰고 성큼성큼 걸어 들어갔지요.
pages.t: And right at that moment, Tteokbo — who had just carried a big earthenware steamer into the palace kitchen — stretched his neck through the crack in the door to watch. "Hand signs? Why, I'm rather good at those!" An old minister's eyes flew wide open. "That's it! You there, go and give it a try!" Tteokbo pulled his straw hat down snug and went striding right in.

pages.ko: 사신이 떡보 앞에 마주 앉았어요. 그러고는 손가락으로 커다란 동그라미를 슥— 그렸지요. '하늘은 둥글다. 그대는 아는가?' 하는 뜻이었어요. 그런데 떡보의 눈이 반짝! "오호, 동그란 절편 말이군요!"
pages.t: The envoy sat down face to face with Tteokbo. Then, with one finger, he drew a great big circle in the air. He meant, 'The sky is round. Do you know this?' But Tteokbo's eyes went sparkle! "Oho, you mean a nice round rice cake!"

pages.ko: 떡보는 두 손으로 네모를 척! 그렸어요. "나는 네모난 백설기가 더 좋소이다!" 그러자 사신이 무릎을 탁 쳤어요. '하늘은 둥글고 땅은 네모나다! 옳은 말씀이오!' 신하들은 어리둥절, 눈만 껌뻑였답니다.
pages.t: Tteokbo drew a square with both hands — snap! "Well, I like square white rice cakes better!" At that, the envoy slapped his knee. 'The sky is round and the earth is square! Quite right, quite right!' The ministers just blinked and blinked, not understanding a thing.

pages.ko: 이번엔 사신이 손가락 셋을 쫙 펴 보였어요. '사람이 지켜야 할 세 가지를 아는가?' 하는 뜻이었지요. 떡보는 볼록한 배를 쓱 문질렀어요. "아침에 떡을 셋 먹었느냐고요? 에이, 그것보다 훨씬 많지요!"
pages.t: Next the envoy held up three fingers. He meant, 'Do you know the three things a person must always keep?' Tteokbo rubbed his round belly. "You're asking if I ate three rice cakes this morning? Oh no, far more than that!"

pages.ko: 떡보는 손가락 다섯을 활짝 펴며 신나게 외쳤어요. "떡 하나 쿵! 떡 둘 쿵! 세어 보자, 배가 통통!" 다섯 손가락을 본 사신은 크게 감탄했어요. '셋도 모자라 다섯까지 헤아리다니, 참으로 깊구나!'
pages.t: Tteokbo spread out all five fingers and shouted merrily, "One rice cake, thump! Two rice cakes, thump! Count them up — my belly goes plump!" When the envoy saw those five fingers, he was full of wonder. 'Not three, but five he counts! How very deep this man is!'

pages.ko: 마지막으로 사신이 손바닥을 활짝 펴 위를 가리켰어요. '하늘의 뜻을 아는가?' 하는 아주 어려운 물음이었지요. 대전 안이 쥐 죽은 듯 조용해졌어요. 떡보는 고개를 갸웃했어요. "위요? 위에서 뭘 먹었느냐고요?"
pages.t: Last of all, the envoy opened his palm wide and pointed upward. It was a very hard question: 'Do you know the will of heaven?' The great hall went as quiet as a mouse. Tteokbo tilted his head. "Up there? You're asking what I ate up there?"

pages.ko: 떡보는 볼록한 배를 통통 두드리더니, 손가락으로 아래를 쏙 가리켰어요. "떡은 여기, 뱃속으로 쏙 내려갔지요!" 사신의 눈이 휘둥그레졌어요. '하늘의 뜻이 땅에까지 닿는다는 말씀이로구나!'
pages.t: Tteokbo patted his round belly — pat, pat — and then pointed one finger downward. "The rice cakes went down here, right into my tummy!" The envoy's eyes went round as saucers. 'He means the will of heaven reaches all the way down to the earth!'

pages.ko: 사신은 자리에서 벌떡 일어나 떡보에게 허리를 깊이 숙였어요. 그러고는 처음으로 입을 열었지요. "이 나라에는 참으로 훌륭한 분이 계시는군요!" 그러고는 환하게 웃으며 돌아갔답니다. 신하들은 얼싸안고 만세를 불렀어요. "만세! 떡보 만세!"
pages.t: The envoy jumped up from his seat and bowed deeply to Tteokbo. And then, for the very first time, he opened his mouth. "Truly, this country has a most wonderful man!" And away he went, smiling a bright, happy smile. The ministers hugged one another and cheered. "Hooray! Hooray for Tteokbo!"

pages.ko: "그래, 그 손짓들은 대체 무슨 뜻이었느냐?" 임금님이 묻자 떡보는 머리를 긁적였어요. "손짓이요? 저는… 떡 이야기만 했는뎁쇼?" 궁궐이 온통 웃음바다가 되었지요. 임금님은 찬합 가득 떡을 담아 주었고, 떡보는 신이 나서 또 노래했어요. "떡 하나 쿵! 떡 둘 쿵! 세어 보자, 배가 통통!" 모르면 모르는 대로 씩씩하게 나서면, 웃음이 길을 열어 준대요.
pages.t: "Now tell me — what did all those hand signs mean?" asked the king. Tteokbo scratched his head. "Hand signs? I… I was only talking about rice cakes." The whole palace burst into a sea of laughter. The king filled a stacked picnic box to the brim with rice cakes for him, and Tteokbo sang again, happy as could be. "One rice cake, thump! Two rice cakes, thump! Count them up — my belly goes plump!" They say if you step up bravely even when you don't know a thing, laughter will open the road for you.
